Task 410 research dispatch died on an API server error mid-response; .return-meta.json left at status=in_progress with no report written.

recovery.suggested_action: Re-dispatch research for task 410; status reset to not_started so it is eligible again.

errors.message: literature-ingest-online.sh Zotero create-item step fails with ONLINE_INGEST_ZOTERO_CREATE_FAILED, caused by TypeError: 'httpx.Timeout' object cannot be interpreted as an integer or float inside the zotero-cli-cc -> pyzotero -> httpx2/httpcore2 dependency chain. This is version-drift in the dependency, independent of any source's availability.

context.observed_consequence: Every new open-access ingest must bypass the Zotero write step; documents ingested that way carry zotero_key: null and zotero_path: null in the global Literature index. gehrke_jonsson_2004 (registered 2026-09-18) is the current example.

recovery.suggested_action: meta task: pin or patch the zotero-cli-cc dependency versions (pyzotero/httpx2/httpcore2) to resolve the httpx.Timeout TypeError.
recovery.workaround: Download and magic-byte-verify the PDF, feed it directly to the unmodified literature-ingest.sh (bypassing the Zotero write step), then patch the global index metadata by hand against an existing entry's schema. Manual, not automated.

errors.message: Lake treated 24 of 638 FormalSystem .olean artifacts as current although their sources were newer, so current sources were elaborated against an older revision of their dependencies. PlusSlicedCertificate/Basic.olean was dated 2026-10-01 10:41 against a source committed 2026-10-02 01:51 and contained zero occurrences of 'decoded'. A plain 'lake build' did NOT repair it and neither did touching the source: the recorded trace matched, so lake skipped recompilation. Symptom was a spurious build failure in PlusSlicedCertificate/Window.lean (16 errors: Invalid field 'decoded'/'decoded_neg'/'decoded_fwd' and two 'does not contain' failures on exists_combined_window_eq/exists_win_eq), which read as a code defect at HEAD but was not one -- the source tree was correct throughout.

context.diagnostic_tell: PlusGraphPath.lab and .st resolved while PlusGraphPath.decoded did not, even though lab and st are defined AS (P.decoded t).1/.2. A file cannot compile lab without decoded, so the olean and the source provably came from different revisions. That asymmetry is the cheapest signal that a cache is inconsistent rather than that code is broken.
context.observed_consequence: Silent corruption of verification evidence, not just a failed build. A probe evaluated a LANDED Stable.TailStable theorem as FALSE against the stale cache, which could have been mistaken for a refutation. Research agents verifying claims by running the build in this window produced unreliable results; claims verified by reading source were unaffected.

recovery.suggested_action: Add a cheap staleness probe to the Lean acceptance gates: for each FormalSystem source, fail if its .olean is older than the source. That is the check that would have caught this before five research dispatches ran against it.
recovery.workaround: Delete the stale artifacts so lake must re-elaborate, rather than trusting 'lake build' or touch: rm the .olean/.trace/.ilean plus the ir/*.c and ir/*.c.trace for every module whose source is newer than its .olean, then 'lake build'. Verified: full rebuild green at 2806 jobs, zero errors, zero sorries, 0 remaining stale oleans, and all five previously-unresolved symbols resolve. A full 'lake clean' is unnecessary and would rebuild dependencies.
